chunks: Here you are, those who love them but they do not love you, and you believe in the whole Book; when they meet you they say, 'We believe,' but when they are alone they bite their fingers at you in rage. Say, 'Die of your rage; indeed, Allah is Knower of that within the breasts.'

key_terms.ذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ: that within the breasts (secrets of the heart)

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'bite their fingers in rage' signify in the context of the hypocrites in Surah Aal-Imran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often linked to the Hypocrites (Munafiqun) who outwardly professed Islam but harbored deep-seated enmity, particularly noted in the context of the Battle of Uhud and the subsequent siege of Medina. The phrase 'bite their fingers in rage' vividly captures their internal frustration at being exposed, while the command 'die of your rage' serves as a divine assurance that their anger cannot harm the believers. This highlights the Shia emphasis on distinguishing between true faith (Iman) and mere outward submission (Islam) through the lens of inner sincerity.
